html:
SMTO-BOOT-0034 — Another model server is still using the benchmark's port

GUID: 9f08f8ad-e462-4df7-a0f4-90bc9604f062
Slug: boot-model-shutdown-timeout
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • Before starting each model, the benchmark waits for its port to be free. Something kept answering there for two minutes, so this model wasn't started and gets no score in the report.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look for a terminal window where you started a model server yourself, or an earlier benchmark that's still open. If you no longer need it, press Ctrl+C in that window. A model server left running from earlier is what usually keeps answering on the benchmark's port (18000 unless you chose another with --port).
  2. If you can't find it, run the benchmark on a free port instead, for example by adding --port 18100 to the command. The benchmark only needs an empty port; the other server doesn't have to stop.
  3. Before stopping a program you didn't start, ask the person who manages this computer what it is. It may be someone else's model server doing real work, and stopping it would interrupt them.

What success looks like

  • The benchmark starts that model, and the report in src/vllm/results/ shows a score for it instead of a startup error.

If it still fails

  • Copy this model's section from the benchmark report (the newest benchmark-….md file in src/vllm/results/), including the SMTO-BOOT-0034 code and the address it names, and send it to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't force-stop unknown programs just to free the port.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The vLLM benchmark did not launch the next profile because an endpoint on its port still answered GET /v1/models after the 120-second wait for the port to become free.

What this means

  • Endpoint-absence polling reaches its deadline while the selected model endpoint still answers. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Endpoint-absence polling reaches its deadline while the selected model endpoint still answers.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the actual endpoint owner before starting or stopping another process.

How to fix it

  • Find the listener on the benchmark port (default 18000, for example ss -ltnp 'sport = :18000') and confirm whether it is a leftover vLLM process group from an earlier profile or an unrelated server. Stop only a leftover you own, or rerun with --port set to a free port; wait_for_server_absent polls http://127.0.0.1:18000/v1/models (or the chosen --port) for up to 120 s before each launch, and the failure is recorded in that profile's section of benchmark-*.md/.json rather than printed to the terminal.
  • Inspect the owning process before another launch; stop the intended process through its supported controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended shutdown is confirmed without terminating an unrelated server.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
